I have investigated the codebase, traced the failing test, identified the intended behavior, and documented it in `requirement.feature`.

### Investigation Summary
- **Failing Test**: [`MathUtilsTest.testArrayEquals`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_arch/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtilsTest.java#L442-L463) fails at line 456 on `assertFalse(MathUtils.equals(new double[] { Double.NaN }, new double[] { Double.NaN }))`.
- **Buggy Logic**: In [`MathUtils.equals(double x, double y)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_arch/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L416-L418), comparing two `NaN` values evaluates to `true` (`(Double.isNaN(x) && Double.isNaN(y)) || x == y`). When [`MathUtils.equals(double[] x, double[] y)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_arch/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/util/MathUtils.java#L522-L535) compares arrays element-by-element, two arrays containing `NaN` at matching indices are erroneously considered equal.
- **Intended Behavior**: According to IEEE 754 and the specification of standard `equals` methods in Commons Math, `NaN` is not equal to `NaN`. Comparing two `NaN` double values, or two arrays containing `NaN` values, should return `false`.

The specification has been saved to [`requirement.feature`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_63_group_d_arch/requirement.feature).
